anchors.paper_title: An EEG-based Imagined Speech Database for comparing Paradigm Designs
anchors.reason: Scientific Data descriptor with matching authors, 15 volunteers (7 female), and the traditional vs video-game imagined speech paradigm comparison, which is this dataset's source data.

metadata.methods_description: EEG was acquired from 15 healthy participants (ages 18-27) with a 24-channel mBrainTrain Smarting system at 500 Hz, FCz reference and Fpz ground. The traditional paradigm used visual and auditory cues (5 beeps at 1.4 s rhythm) followed by 7 imagined speech repetitions, of which the last 3 were kept. The gamified paradigm used a Pac-Man maze interface with 1.4 s periods for movement decision, imagined speech, and vocalized speech. Each participant completed 120 trials per session (30 per class).

citation_details.title: Interpretable Brain-computer Interface for Emotion-aware Thought-to-speech using Eeg Signal Decoding
citation_details.author: Abhimanyu Singh, Edith Paulin S
citation_details.abstract: Restoring effective communication for people with severe speech impairment remains a most important concern in assistive healthcare. Electroencephalography (EEG)-Based Brain–Computer Interfaces (BCI) can decode imagined speech from neural activity; however, existing techniques have been limited by a lack of interpretability, reduced robustness across users, and inadequate integration of emotional context. In this study, we present an Interpretable Brain–Computer Interface for Emotion-Aware Thought-to-Speech that incorporates affective state recognition, EEG signal decoding, and explainable deep learning within a unified framework. The presented framework combines advanced EEG preprocessing, spatio-temporal feature representation, attention-guided neural learning, and an explainability module while identifying the underlying neural features and cortical regions influencing each prediction.
